name: rsi_extreme_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: RSI(2) on 1-min bars reaches extreme levels (<5 or >95) relatively frequently and these extremes revert quickly. The very short 2-period RSI captures momentum exhaustion at the micro level — when RSI(2) < 5, price has closed lower than the previous close for 2 consecutive bars with large magnitude, indicating a short-term selling climax. Larry Connors' research on RSI(2) for daily bars showed mean reversion at extremes; the same logic applies to 1-min bars but with faster reversion. The edge exists because RSI(2) signals at the 1-min level are too fast for manual traders and the profit per trade is too small for institutional attention. Indian markets have higher retail participation, which creates more noisy overshoots.

long.confirmation: RSI(close, 2) crosses above 10 (initial bounce from extreme)

short.confirmation: RSI(close, 2) crosses below 90 (initial pullback from extreme)

exit.target: RSI(close, 2) crosses 60 (longs) or crosses 40 (shorts) — momentum normalized
exit.stop_loss: 0.2% from entry (tight stop for short-duration trades)
exit.trailing_stop: none — trades are too short for trailing stops to add value
exit.signal_exit: exit if RSI(close, 2) makes new extreme (below 3 for longs, above 97 for shorts)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; reduce to 50K after 3 consecutive losses

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; RSI extremes are less reliable in panic
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:45 (fast trades ok late in day)
filters.trend_filter: RSI(14) between 30-70 ensures we are not fighting a strong trend
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask spread < 0.04% (tight spread essential for scalp-like trades)
filters.event_filter: skip on earnings day for that stock
other_filters: max 2 trades in same stock in same direction within 30 min (avoid overtrading one name)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — RSI(2) reversion is well-documented but speed barrier exists on 1-min

weaknesses: Very high trade frequency (4-8/day) means costs eat the edge — need extremely tight execution
RSI(2) on 1-min bars is essentially a 2-bar momentum oscillator, extremely noisy, prone to whipsaws
Average winner is smaller than average loser (W:L = 0.8) — relies heavily on high win rate; a slight win rate drop makes strategy unprofitable
prior_art: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez ('Short-Term Trading Strategies That Work') extensively studied RSI(2) for daily bars. Connors found RSI(2)<5 had ~85% reversion rate on daily S&P 500 stocks. Adaptation to 1-min bars is less documented. Indian market application is novel.
notes: Edge math: 0.65 * 18bps - 0.35 * 22.5bps = 11.7 - 7.9 = 3.8 bps gross per trade. Costs ~11 bps per round trip. Net ≈ -7.2 bps. Significantly negative. This strategy as described is NOT profitable after costs. High trade frequency makes it worse. REQUIRES: (1) reduce costs via direct market access, (2) increase per-trade edge by filtering for only highest-conviction RSI(2) extremes, (3) consider RSI(3) instead for slightly longer holds. Included as research hypothesis — needs significant optimization to be viable.
